derivations.quote: Hence $\Phi(f)\le (s/W)\Phi(f/m)+O(f^\tau+1)$ with $\Phi(1)=O(1)$, since the children cost $s(V/W)\Phi(f/m)$ and dividing by $V$ gives $s/W$. Since $s/W<m$, some rational $\tau<1$ gives $(s/W)/m^\tau<1$; this is where $s<Wm$ is used. Dividing by $m^{k\tau}$ gives $m^{-k\tau}\Phi(m^k)\le \frac{s/W}{m^\tau}\,m^{-(k-1)\tau}\Phi(m^{k-1})+O(1)$, since $f^\tau+1\le 2f^\tau$. Unrolling gives a geometric sum with ratio $(s/W)/m^\tau<1$, so $\Phi(m^k)=O(m^{k\tau})$. A field of $f$ radix-$q$ digits has $\Theta(f)$ bits, because $q$ is fixed, so $f$ is proportional to $u$ and the interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$. The butterfly layer uses a second fixed network, also with $s<Wm$, and runs the same recursion on the $d$ selected chunks, so it costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ once $\lambda'$ exceeds two exponents. Nodes with at least $\sqrt d$ active chunks have node overhead of $O(f^\lambda)$ per unit volume, with $f\le d$ and $\lambda=1-2^{-52}$. Smaller nodes, the small-level leaves, cost $O(d^{\sigma+(1-\sigma)/2})$ with $\sigma=1-2^{-50}$. So $\lambda'$ must exceed $\lambda$ and $\sigma+(1-\sigma)/2$, and $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$ does.

relations.quote: The machine performs its address moves by [Fast interchange of address fields](fast-address-interchange.md).
It performs its butterfly layers by [Fast simultaneous butterfly layers](fast-butterfly-layers.md).
The machine computes its convolution by [Convolution with retained transform order and cancelled permutations](ring-convolution-retained-order.md).
The machine recovers its coefficients by [Fixed-point precision and exact recovery](fixed-point-precision.md).
It disproves the [n log n optimality conjecture](nlogn-conjecture.md) for this model.
The machine places its coefficient list by the [Chinese-remainder map to prime cyclic axes](crt-address-map.md).
